name: Senegalia

project_scope.selection_mode: Master Plant Pool field-ID comparison; not automatically a canonical species install
project_scope.native_range_status: All three Texas native at state level; 3-target-county verification unresolved. No invented county PASS.
project_scope.primary_local_anchor: Senegalia roemeriana — Hays flora confirms wild local occurrence
project_scope.current_status: All three Senegalia species now installed in canonical manifest; roemeriana has 2 physical images, wrightii 1, greggii 2. Scientific native-range decisions remain independent and unresolved.

look_here_first: 1) Look for hooked PRICKLES on the woody twig. 2) Compare the flower cluster: ROUND cream head = S. roemeriana; elongated cream SPIKE = S. greggii or S. wrightii. 3) For Gregg versus Wright, measure several leaflets and petioles and inspect mature pods; no single size or pod curl is an absolute species test.

shared_traits: Thorny woody members of the mimosoid legume clade with alternate BIPINNATE leaves.
Sharp hooked prickles occur along branches, unlike paired straight stipular spines typical of Vachellia.
Flower clusters of many tiny staminate-looking flowers, often cream to white, are HEADS in one local species and SPIKES in the others.
Flattened legumes; mature pod constriction, curling and width can help but vary, so use multiple traits.
priority: LOOK 1: globose pale inflorescences versus elongated spikes (the quickest split).
LOOK 2: identify strongly hooked stem PRICKLES, contrasting paired straight Vachellia spines.
LOOK 3: Wright's dry pods show flattened bulges separated by deep constrictions, but pod outline varies and is not an absolute species split.
LOOK 4: Wright typically has larger/broader mature leaflets than Gregg; only use photographs with matching real scales for measurement.
LOOK 5: Gregg generally has denser spikes and may have more strongly curled ripe pods, but overlapping key characters require combinations.
FINAL FINE PASS: macro of petiole glands, fully isolated prickle insertion, same-mm-ruler Gregg vs Wright leaflets, and additional mature pod comparisons.
study_strategy.warning: Texas A&M and a 2024 morphology key differ somewhat in numeric leaflet ranges for Wright catclaw. Both agree Wright tends to have larger leaflets than Gregg; avoid exact cutoff without examining several leaves. S. roemeriana is taxonomically distinct from Senna roemeriana (twoleaf senna), despite sharing species epithet.

quick_key.if: round or nearly spherical pale cream flower HEAD and hooked prickles
elongated cream flower SPIKE and small numerous obovate leaflets (typically smaller than Wright), dense spike
elongated cream flower SPIKE but noticeably broader/larger obovate leaflets, somewhat looser spike
quick_key.then: Senegalia wrightii — Wright acacia; confirm with mature pods

quick_key.if: yellow/gold spherical flower heads, paired straight stipular spines at leaf node
quick_key.then: Vachellia constricta or V. farnesiana, NOT Senegalia

quick_key.if: yellow flowers with five large distinct petals and exactly 1 pair of broad compound leaflets
quick_key.then: Senna roemeriana and relatives — DIFFERENT genus

comparison_matrix.roemeriana: Spherical pale cream capitulum (<2× as long as broad)
comparison_matrix.greggii: Dense, cream cylindrical spike (2–6× as long as broad)
comparison_matrix.wrightii: Often lax / less dense pale cylinder (2–6× as long as broad)

comparison_matrix.weight: High-value supporting trait, overlap from 5–6 mm

comparison_matrix.roemeriana: Usually 2–4 pinna pairs, 6–13 leaflet pairs per pinna
comparison_matrix.greggii: Several pairs, often smaller obovate leaflets; source-key detailed count not yet reconciled
comparison_matrix.wrightii: Usually 1–4 pinna pairs, 3–6 leaflet pairs per pinna
Frequently straighter in regional key, BUT morphology description allows coiled pods

comparison_matrix.weight: Genus cue, not diagnostic within these three

comparison_matrix.roemeriana: Use full reproductive specimen if ambiguous
comparison_matrix.wrightii: Do not force species if intermediate

visual_comparison.title: Three catclaws: flower clusters, prickles, leaflets, and pods
visual_comparison.subtitle: Use the exact-species Gregg and Wright foliage photographs as a SHAPE comparison, NOT a measured size comparison. Both photos have different camera scales. Rounded cream heads distinguish Roemer's; elongated pale spikes lead to Gregg/Wright.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: ROEMER = nearly round cream heads. GREGG vs WRIGHT = elongated spikes; compare several leaflets against real millimeter rulers and look at pod traits together.

diagnostic_photo_checklist: All three: recurved thorn placement relative to twig node, matched close-up
S. roemeriana: globose flowerhead and a complete bipinnate leaf
S. greggii versus S. wrightii: same scale pinnules/leaflets with millimeter ruler
Gregg and Wright: ripe pod twisting and segment shape photographed alongside leaves
Petiole nectary gland macro for each species
Wright alternative licensed habit and ripe pod; first bloom face is ready

scientific_cautions.point: Wright vs Gregg reported hybridization and variable characters
scientific_cautions.explanation: Published hybrids among Senegalia berlandieri, S. greggii and S. wrightii in Texas / adjacent Mexico have been reported. Mixed or intermediate characters deserve a provisional Senegalia sp. identification, not an automatic species label.
scientific_cautions.source: Seigler, Ebinger & Glass 2012, Phytologia 94:439–455; cited in peer-reviewed 2024 regional flora, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10857220/.

scientific_cautions: Arizona Campus Arboretum 2025 illustrates Wright catclaw with curling maturing pods too; therefore a curved pod alone cannot distinguish Gregg from Wright. Green/pink Gregg pod photo is developing, not fully mature.

photo_next_pass.completed: All three source-pool Senegalia species have exact-source physical photos. Gregg has 6 including hooked prickles, cream spike, seeds with 1 cm ruler, full leafy branch, and new attached developing curled pods; Wright has 3 incl. ripe Uvalde pods; Roemer has 6.
prioritized_missing: Gregg versus Wright: independently verified adult leaflets, each photographed with a physical millimeter ruler (matching scales)
Wright: single close in-focus hooked prickle with clear placement on stem/twig, rights cleared for reuse
Gregg: attached FULLY DRY mature pods with identity-confirming foliage and physical ruler; compare to existing Wright Uvalde dry pods, do not use curling as absolute criterion
